claim: A bracket inside a string value of a dropped table (e.g. command = "foo[") is counted as an open array, so lean_config swallows the following lines, including the kept [profiles.p] table.
what_goes_wrong: A '[' inside a string value in a dropped table (e.g. an mcp_servers command or args entry) leaves skip_depth positive, so every following line, including kept tables like [profiles.p], is silently dropped from the worker's lean config.toml.
fix_idea: End skip_depth when a line matches a table header (as the kept_depth path does), and count only brackets outside quoted strings and comments.

claim: The flow id built in fix_graph does not include the bug ids of the group, although the task text differs. Two fix runs of the same file with different bugs (e.g. --only) get the same graph id.
what_goes_wrong: Two fix runs of the same file with different bug sets (cmd_fix --only) get the same graph id, so the second run overwrites the stored graph file <id>.json and the first run's record['graph'] then points to a graph whose task text lists other bugs.
fix_idea: Add the sorted bug ids of g["bugs"] to the digest that builds fid in fix_graph, as cmd_fix does for the run id.

claim: An explicit path such as './pkg' passes the presence check (git resolves it) but is stored unnormalized, so in_paths and the git diff pathspecs never match 'pkg/...' files; only trailing slashes are cleaned.
what_goes_wrong: A user passing --paths ./pkg gets './pkg' stored in audit.json, so in_paths never matches 'pkg/...' files and changed-function targets are silently dropped.
fix_idea: Normalize each path with posixpath.normpath (dropping a leading './') before the presence check and before storing.

claim: import_root './src' is only stripped of slashes, so it is stored as './src' and the package path becomes './src/pkg'; top_of and run_snippet then misbehave.
what_goes_wrong: A user passing --import-root ./src gets './src' stored, so top_of never strips the root (file names are 'src/...') and package paths become './src/pkg', giving wrong top names and snippets.
fix_idea: Normalize import_root with posixpath.normpath and strip any leading './' before use.

claim: git writes a trailing tab after a path that contains a space in the ---/+++ header lines. parse_diff keeps the tab in the path, so the file cannot be found.
what_goes_wrong: A changed .py file whose path contains a space gets a trailing tab in its path, so in_paths/git show fail and the changed functions of that file are silently not targeted.
fix_idea: Strip the trailing tab from the header path (rstrip('\t')), or run git diff with -z / parse the diff --git line.

claim: git quotes paths with non-ASCII characters in the ---/+++ headers, as "a/\303\251.py". parse_diff strips two characters and leaves a stray quote, giving a wrong path.
what_goes_wrong: With git's default core.quotepath, a changed file with a non-ASCII name appears as a quoted octal path, which parse_diff turns into a garbage path (stray quote, no a/ strip), so that file is skipped by cmd_targets --changed.
fix_idea: Pass -c core.quotepath=false to git diff and unquote C-style quoted paths (strip quotes, decode escapes) before removing the a/ b/ prefix.

claim: The search for related tests misses a test file that imports the changed module with a top-level `from mod import x` (no dot, module not in the file name), so its failing tests are never run and the fix is accepted.
what_goes_wrong: A repository test file that does `from mod import f` (flat layout, module not in file name) is not selected as related, so a fix that breaks it is accepted instead of rejected.
fix_idea: Also match a `from <dotted path ending in stem> import ...` line in the related-test regex.
